scope: Completed fixed 20 V5 arms paired against completed old V3/V4. Read-only offline mechanism audit, not a new simulation or training run.

executor_invalid_search_starvation.mechanism_status: Source-derived deterministic event-priority chain plus directly observed trace/query states; no intervention was run to estimate its effect on Found.
source_chain: event_detector.py:162-165 marks the standby executor invalid whenever the retained executor assignment is unreachable; :293-296 emits EXECUTOR_INVALID and also WAYPOINT_STALE when searchers have reached their goals.
hysteresis/policy.py:14-21 prioritizes EXECUTOR_INVALID before WAYPOINT_STALE. online/controller.py:335-344 returns the whole previous allocation when that primary event is in cooldown.

online/controller.py:376-397 handles pre-Found EXECUTOR_INVALID using executor_only allocation with affected_searcher_ids=(). When it proposes no assignment change, :488-495 marks that attempt and returns without search allocation.
online/config.py:71-75 sets executor invalid cooldown to the state refresh cadence, which is 20 in the loaded corrected configuration. This is distinct from 5-step search failure retry.
safe_search_v1/runtime.py:96-129 only adds independent affected-searcher recovery when failure_policy is enabled. V5 disables it; V4 enables it. No production behavior was changed in this audit.

V4_same_standby_failure_counterexample.causal_limit: V4 proves an existing independent recovery route can bypass this scheduling stall in the paired case; V4 also does not Found, so restored movement is not proof of detection improvement.

executor_invalid_search_starvation.next_priority: Implement an opt-in Chapter 3 separation of pre-Found standby-invalid handling and search recovery scheduling; a waiting executor must not suppress an eligible searcher replacement. Retain public-state boundaries and post-Found handoff/execution contracts. Validate the index97/10 mechanism first, then fixed20 full paired ablation. Do not claim that avoiding stall guarantees recovering either lost Found.

new_collision_index77.minimal_supported_conclusion: Agent 0 receives a new route at 279 while speed is 1.762347 and velocity-to-tracking angle is 80.807 degrees; at 280 angle is 92.408 degrees and speed 1.450626. It enters hold at 281 with speed 1.142357 after an invalid_start safety repair query, then collides at 282. The terminal safety label is UNVERIFIED_BRAKING. This supports testing braking/turn-aware speed limits; it does not establish when the obstacle was first observed or that a map flip caused this collision.
new_collision_index77.causal_limit: V4 and V5 physical trajectories diverge at 22, long before V4 Found130. Do not attribute lost detection to the final collision alone or to one early local event.

other_lost_case_index67.interpretation: V5 has little measured motion stall but still loses V4 discovery. Different timing/route/observation histories can change encounter with a moving target; no unique detection-failure cause is proven from these traces.

interpretive_limits: decision_reason counts are counts of captured after-state labels, not necessarily independent fresh decision invocations; terminal states may retain the preceding label. Query counts are separately checked.
Completed-goal waiting is counted in contiguous states satisfying tracker_completed, not hold, pre-Found and distance<=0.75. It is not the existing motion-stall metric and not zero sensor capability.
No hidden target or obstacle-map queries were made. Collision records are already present terminal diagnostic data.
Live cell probabilities/first observation timestamps are unavailable for the new collision; no fresh-occupancy replay was performed.
Comparisons are paired developmental outcomes on the fixed20, not final heldout evidence or statistical proof. No new intervention establishes the individual causal contribution to Found.
